title: Click and observe
summary: A click asks the browser to activate a control. Check the resulting page state.
introduction: A click asks the browser to activate a control. Check the resulting page state. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A click asks the browser to activate a control. Check the resulting page state.

blocks.code:
from urllib.parse import quote
from selenium import webdriver
from selenium.webdriver.common.by import By

driver = webdriver.Chrome()
try:
    driver.get("data:text/html;charset=utf-8," + quote('<button id="save" onclick="this.textContent=\'Done\'">Save</button>'))
    driver.find_element(By.ID, "save").click()
    assert driver.find_element(By.ID, "save").text == "Done"
finally:
    driver.quit()
blocks.title: Click and observe

blocks.text: After the click, the button reads Done.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Change the action to write Saved.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: A click alone does not prove the intended action completed.
For more detail later, use this [Selenium further reading](https://www.selenium.dev/documentation/webdriver/).
